parsed.main_gap: Key lemma asserts a graph with q vertices and ≤ q−1 edges is a forest (false); needs only 'some component is a tree', an immediate one-line fix.

errors.description: In the refinement lemma's lower bound, the multigraph has q vertices and ≤ q−1 edges, but this does NOT imply acyclicity: a component may contain a cycle or loop provided another component compensates (e.g. triangle + isolated vertex, 4 vertices, 3 edges). The correct deduction is only that SOME component is a tree; the write-up instead claims all components are trees and then selects the (possibly non-tree) component of a_q.
errors.quote:
Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains
no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on \(v\) vertices already uses at
least \(v\) edges; hence every connected component \(C\) has \(e_C=v_C-1\) and
is a tree

errors.description: Consequent to the above: the component actually used is picked arbitrarily ('containing the vertex of a_q') with no argument that it is a tree, so the bipartition/sign assignment underlying inequality (3) is not justified as written. (Any tree component would work, so the repair is immediate.)
errors.quote:
We use the component
containing the vertex of \(a_q\).

parsed.notes: Correct answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1); drafting lemma, subset-sum pigeonhole, overlay construction for Xiang, and Liu's binary construction are all correct and carefully done. Section 5 is extraneous but harmless. Only the forest claim is flawed.
